findings.body: Raise: Functional. This new no-worktree advice is unreachable in `forge next` for a part that exists only on a fetched remote branch. `_task` returns an empty state when there is no local worktree (`nextstep.py:598`), and `_story` calls `_item` only for nonempty states (`nextstep.py:453–458`). A second clone can therefore show the part as ready in `forge board --json` while `forge next` offers to start it instead of naming its starter.
findings.title: Not done: forge next omits ready parts without a worktree

findings.body: Raise: Functional. `forge next` does not fetch before `_item` calls `at_ref`. After another machine pushes a reviewed commit, GitHub supplies its new `headRefOid`, but this clone may not have that Git object. `story.show` then finds no state and this fallback keeps the older worktree's findings and round. The new test calls `forge board` first, whose fetch masks this normal `forge next` path.
findings.title: Not done: forge next must fetch a newer review head before reading it

findings.body: Raise: Not done. `approved` checks only `story.approval_hash`, which covers “What changes for you” and “Done when” (`story.py:645–654`). Editing another section above `## For the builders`, such as Why or Tasks, leaves that hash unchanged but makes `story.gate` fail (`story.py:671–684`). This branch still counts the story as approved or building while `forge next` requires another read. The added test edits a hashed section, so it does not catch this case.
findings.title: Not done: approval counting must honor a stale cold read

findings.body: Raise: Test. The GitHub-failure case asserts only that the fixes count object exists. That object exists without GitHub, so the test would pass if a failed fetch exposed stale PR facts instead of marking GitHub facts unknown. The Done-when rule explicitly requires the failure result to be unknown in `forge board --json`.
findings.title: Not done: test_board_github_once verifies unknown facts on failure

findings.body: Raise: Gate. The supplied proof list has five headings with no proof beneath any of them. It identifies no runnable check or result for counts, review-head history, cached GitHub reads, approval counts, or the complete story runway, so the required proof entries are missing.
findings.title: Not done: proof list
